# Tokenomics of Outcome

Status: working research note

Purpose: define how the ROI dashboard should reason about
token cost for a correct workflow outcome.

Core question:

> What did it cost, in tokens, to produce the correct outcome
> for a specific workflow intent?

## Core Issue

Raw token spend is not enough.

The unit of measurement must be:

```text
intent -> execution path -> terminal state -> outcome quality
```

There are two distinct measurements.

| Layer | Question |
|---|---|
| Task completion | Did the workflow reach its intended terminal state? |
| Outcome quality | Was the terminal state correct and valuable? |

Task completion measures completion, abandonment, drift, and waste.
Outcome quality measures whether token spend created net business value.

Task completion says whether the workflow got somewhere.

Outcome quality says whether it got to the right place.

# Talium Documentation Style

Status: repo-local working guide

Purpose: capture documentation preferences for Talium product,
research, and design notes.

## Principles

- Start with the core issue.
- Separate open questions from the main draft.
- Ask clarifying questions in chat before editing.
- Keep documents terse, readable, and information dense.
- Prefer strong information organization over longer prose.
- Use examples only when they clarify a concept quickly.
- Put data models and implementation fields near the end.
- Put references at the end.

## Structure

Use this default order for research/design notes:

```text
1. Core issue
2. Proposed framing or measurement approach
3. Visual model, if useful
4. Compact explanation of each component
5. Options, tradeoffs, or method comparison
6. Dashboard or product implications, if discussed
7. Data model
8. References
```

Avoid putting unresolved clarifying questions in the main document.
Use chat first, or a separate questions file …[TRUNCATED]

Ok the distilled classifier Human labelling etc. should be all in one section. 
It is a big area, labeling systems are no joke. The talium project will not be involved in labeling at all. It assumes that labeled set exists and then wants to compare the runs against labeled set.

* A distilled model may exists. In that case use it. 
* If there is not distilled model then idea would be to use the path graph of good run vs bad run. I realize this is not always possible, not every agent action uses tools. Somtime tools like serach web is meaningless without the context. 

The key is that we are not in the buiness of creating labelled data set At least now. If a human eval exists then we want to use that.

questions.question: Who is the primary viewer of the dashboard's top level, and what single decision should it drive?

options.label: Buyer / executive
options.description: Economic owner deciding scale / throttle / kill. Top level is a crisp verdict (ROI, value vs. baseline, success rate). Detail lives behind drill-down. Optimizes for 'is this worth it?'

options.label: Operator / workflow owner
options.description: Engineer/ops optimizing a live fleet. Top level surfaces waste, failing steps, model/route problems. Optimizes for 'where is the money leaking and why?'

options.label: Both, one layered view
options.description: Single dashboard: executive verdict on top, operator drill-down beneath. Harder to design well but matches 'crisp value + users always want detail.'
